ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #17 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word is the opposite of plump? (1 mark)
   A. healthy
   B. big
   C. thin
   D. round

2. Which sentence would be a good first sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Thank you.
   B. On Saturday, Mama took me to the supermarket.
   C. The end.
   D. Yours lovingly.

3. The inbox is where (1 mark)
   A. the keyboard is stored
   B. messages you receive are kept
   C. messages waiting to be sent are kept
   D. deleted files are burnt

4. In the safety dialogue, why did the message say 'You have won a prize'? (1 mark)
   A. To reward Neema
   B. To help her homework
   C. To teach spelling
   D. It was a trick to steal information

5. Why must an email address be typed carefully? (1 mark)
   A. One wrong letter and the message will not reach the person
   B. It makes the message longer
   C. It makes the screen brighter
   D. It saves paper

6. Quantifiers: Choose the correct sentence. (1 mark)
   A. How much water do you drink?
   B. How many waters do you drink?
   C. How many water do you drink?
   D. How much waters do you drink?

7. What must every sentence begin with? (1 mark)
   A. A comma
   B. A full stop
   C. A capital letter
   D. A question mark

8. What should you do first with a series of pictures? (1 mark)
   A. Draw only one
   B. Write the ending only
   C. Look at all of them and put them in order
   D. Copy a friend

9. What is a stranger? (1 mark)
   A. A close friend
   B. A person you do not know
   C. A person who lives next door
   D. Your teacher

10. Which phrase is a polite way of adding to what someone said? (1 mark)
   A. That is wrong
   B. Stop it now
   C. May I add something?
   D. Be quiet, I am talking

11. What is a rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. Words that start with the same letter
   B. Words that end with the same sound
   C. Words with opposite meanings
   D. Words with the same meaning

12. Choose the correct -ing form of 'play'. (1 mark)
   A. plaing
   B. playying
   C. plaiing
   D. playing

13. Which sentence tells someone to do something and ends with a full stop? (1 mark)
   A. Did you close the door?
   B. What a big door!
   C. Close the door.
   D. The door is red

14. 'It's' is a short form of which words? (1 mark)
   A. its own
   B. it was only
   C. it is or it has
   D. it will only

15. How long should the narrative composition be at this level? (1 mark)
   A. About 60 to 80 words
   B. About 500 words
   C. About 10 words
   D. About 300 words

16. What is a virus? (1 mark)
   A. A sharp tool
   B. A kind of medicine
   C. A tiny germ that can make people ill
   D. A type of food

17. What should you do if you find a needle or razor blade on the ground? (1 mark)
   A. Pick it up and keep it
   B. Not touch it and tell a trusted adult
   C. Play with it
   D. Give it to a younger child

18. In 'The Barber's New Blade', why does the barber use a new blade for each customer? (1 mark)
   A. The blade is red
   B. New blades are cheaper
   C. Customers like blades
   D. Sharing blades can pass germs through blood

19. Which word is an adverb of time? (1 mark)
   A. upstairs
   B. yesterday
   C. quietly
   D. here

20. Which sentence has a comma used correctly before 'but'? (1 mark)
   A. I wanted to go but, it was raining.
   B. I wanted to go, but it was raining.
   C. I wanted, to go but it was raining.
   D. I, wanted to go but it was raining.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain why we do not say 'I am knowing the answer'. Give the correct sentence. (3 marks)

22. Correct: (a) 'How much books are there?' (b) 'I do not have some money.' (2 marks)

23. List three steps to follow before writing a pictorial composition. (3 marks)

24. Sort these adverbs into manner, time and place: quietly, later, nearby, always, neatly, upstairs. (3 marks)

25. Explain the difference between a factual and an inferential question and give an example of each from the story. (4 marks)

26. Put in order: Baraka presses Send; Achieng explains what an email is; they click Compose. (3 marks)

27. Give two things you can add to a pictorial composition that are not in the pictures. (2 marks)

28. Explain what 'prevention' means and use it in a sentence. (3 marks)

29. Explain the difference between intensive and extensive reading. (3 marks)

30. Give the meaning of each word and use it in a sentence: (a) harvest (b) fertilizer. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #17 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — thin
   Plump means fat in a pleasant way and thin is its opposite.

2. B — On Saturday, Mama took me to the supermarket.
   It tells when, who and where.

3. B — messages you receive are kept
   The outbox holds messages waiting to be sent.

4. D — It was a trick to steal information
   The message asked for her name and address.

5. A — One wrong letter and the message will not reach the person
   The address decides where the message goes.

6. A — How much water do you drink?
   Water is uncountable.

7. C — A capital letter
   Capital letters start sentences.

8. C — Look at all of them and put them in order
   You must understand the whole story first.

9. B — A person you do not know
   A stranger is someone you do not know.

10. C — May I add something?
   'May I add something?' asks permission politely.

11. B — Words that end with the same sound
   'Wide' and 'ride' rhyme.

12. D — playing
   A verb ending in y keeps the y before -ing.

13. C — Close the door.
   Commands usually end with a full stop.

14. C — it is or it has
   It's = it is / it has.

15. A — About 60 to 80 words
   The task is a narrative of 60 to 80 words.

16. C — A tiny germ that can make people ill
   A virus is a tiny germ.

17. B — Not touch it and tell a trusted adult
   Sharp objects may carry germs.

18. D — Sharing blades can pass germs through blood
   He explains that blood can carry germs.

19. B — yesterday
   'Yesterday' tells when.

20. B — I wanted to go, but it was raining.
   A comma comes before but when joining two full sentences.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'Know' is a state verb, not an action in progress, so it is not normally used in the progressive form. The correct sentence is 'I know the answer.'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for state verb explanation, 1 for the correct sentence, 1 for clear expression.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) How many books are there? (b) I do not have any money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Look at all the pictures, put them in order, ask who, where and what, make notes, think of a title.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Manner: quietly, neatly. Time: later, always. Place: nearby, upstairs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct group.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: A factual question has its answer stated in the text: 'Where was Omondi's mother?' An inferential question needs clues: 'How did Omondi feel at the start?'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for each example.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Achieng explains what an email is; they click Compose; Baraka presses Send.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct position.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: What people say, and how people feel or think.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Prevention means acting so that something bad does not happen. For example: Washing hands is a way of prevention.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the meaning, 1 for a sentence.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Intensive reading is reading a short text closely, often with the class, to understand it fully. Extensive reading is choosing materials and reading a lot on your own for pleasure and learning.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for the difference in choice or amount.

30. (4 marks)
   Answer: (a) Harvest: to gather crops that are ready. We harvest maize in August. (b) Fertilizer: something added to soil to help plants grow. The farmer put fertilizer on the field.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each word: 1 for the meaning and 1 for a correct sentence.
